Pure argument-inspection predicate — no I/O, no state, no branch imports by design. Runs on every command invocation, so log_operation() here would write a line per CLI call and drown the operation log.

spawn_background() has no in-branch caller BY CONTRACT: the caller is @hooks' lifecycle/auto_process.py, which reaches it cross-branch via importlib.import_module('aipass.memory.apps.handlers.intake.auto_process').spawn_background() - the invocation string is in this file's HOOK ENGINE CONTRACT docstring. Measured 2026-08-13 (DPLAN-0295 item 1): grepped the whole repo for the symbol; the only call site is that hook shell, which @memory may not edit. Same class as the pre-existing 'handlers' rule on this file. Re-verify by grepping spawn_background across src/ - if @hooks' half ships and the symbol has an in-branch caller (e.g. a CLI kick), DELETE this rule.

Cross-branch public API — get_branch_health() wraps detector.check_single_file (entry-count) + lint_handler.run_lint (entry-size) into one function @daemon imports from its modules/ layer, because seedgo blocks handler-to-other-branch-handler imports. THE CALLER HAS LANDED (verified 2026-08-16, DPLAN-0302): daemon/apps/modules/activity_report.py:208 imports it inside _render_entry_health, with daemon/tests/test_activity_report.py:256 patching the same symbol. The earlier version of this rule promised deletion once that happened; that promise was written on a wrong assumption and is retracted. unused_function_check.py declares AUDIT_SCOPE = 'branch_level' and collects .py files with rglob over the BRANCH root only, so it structurally cannot see a caller in another branch — deleting the rule costs 1% forever and teaches nothing. Same permanent class as the 'governance.py' and 'tab_renderer.py' rules above, whose cross-branch callers also exist and are equally invisible. Re-verify by grepping get_branch_health across src/: if the only hits are this branch, the function is genuinely dead and the rule (and the function) should go.

Pure argument-inspection predicate -- no I/O, no state, no branch imports by design, the --json sibling of help_flags.py above. Runs on every command invocation, so log_operation() here would write a line per CLI call and drown the operation log.

Cross-branch entry point the branch-local scan cannot see: @hooks calls it by name via importlib in apps/handlers/security/edit_gate.py (the entry-cap half of the write gate for the whole fleet). Deleting it to satisfy the checker disables that gate. Narrowed to this one function, and the claim is pinned by tests/test_changed_entries.py::TestTheBypassClaimIsMeasuredNotAsserted so the bypass goes red the day @hooks stops calling it.

Bare `todo` IS the verb, by ruling (DPLAN-0345 @memory review section 4, FPLAN-0590 row 5): `drone @memory todo` prints ONE line - pad N of COUNT and the backlog count - so handle_command() deliberately has no no-args gate calling print_introspection(); a gate there would replace that line with the module page. The module still defines print_introspection() (printed after a refused argument) and print_help() (--help/-h/help in any slot). The bare behaviour is pinned by tests/test_config_verbs.py::TestTodoVerbs::test_bare_is_one_line_the_pad_of_the_configured_count_and_the_backlog. Same class as @ai_mail's apps/modules/email.py introspection rule (inbox works without args). Added 2026-09-15; DELETE this rule if bare `todo` ever becomes the introspection page.

File-wide because the checker names no line. apps/__init__.py is the package marker (one line: from . import handlers), not an entry point; the entry point is apps/memory.py, which answers --version / -V (line 315). Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

File-wide because the checker names no line. An empty package marker: it tests no module, so it has no subject line or declared pass to state, and a header on an empty file would be the only content. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

File-wide because the checker names no line. Not a test file: the shared definition of the dead-cwd world that the subprocess pins import (it collects no tests). Its long docstring is why the world exists, and items 6 and 7 of the test template describe a file that tests a module. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The import route is the subject: the helper returns the trigger object through the same import the product makes, because on 3.10 a split worker held two objects and a patch on the other one let a real completion fire (CI run 34088947108). A top-of-file binding is the route that failed. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

File-wide because stdlib_patch passes no line (the checklist calls a lines rule inert); it covers one patch, rr.os.scandir at 659. The only way to make a real directory unlistable for one call without root or platform ACLs. A scandir parameter on exists_exactly would be a door for the test alone (no caller passes it), so the patch stays: monkeypatch scopes it to this test and restores it, and the test asserts the denied listing was the parent. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @devpulse's landing ruling; made file-wide in leg 10.

File-wide because stdlib_patch passes no line; it covers two opt-in fixtures, case_insensitive_filesystem (Path.glob, 414) and case_insensitive_exists (Path.exists, 443). They emulate what Windows and macOS answer so the case-fold pins go red on Linux before CI. Every walk must see the emulation the way it sees the platform, so a product seam per walk would be a door for the tests alone, and Linux cannot show the effect on disk. monkeypatch restores both after each test that asks for them. Leg 10 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The import is what is under test: the parked symbolic package (the owner's ruling of 2026-08-14) must refuse every import, the package and each submodule, naming the ruling. A top-of-file import would raise at collection and pin nothing. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The test is about the import itself: it proves conftest's mock still shadows json_handler through `from X import y` at call time. A top-of-file import would bind before the autouse fixture runs and test nothing. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The trigger bus package is stood in through sys.modules because the test pins the event _announce_bump fires through its own `from aipass.trigger.apps.modules.core import trigger`; the next line asserts that import reaches the stand-in. It is the only edge between @memory and @trigger's bus that keeps a real event from firing. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The subject is import time: memory_files is evicted and imported fresh to prove a removed attribute is not re-created by a fresh import. A top-of-file binding is the already-imported module and could not see that. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_reclaim_stale_lock answers 'is the lane free now'. False after a failed unlink means the lane is NOT free, which is true; the caller's decision (do not run) is the same as for a live lock, and the failure is logged at error. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_is_stale answers 'process this plan again?'. True when the mtime cannot be compared is the decision, not a failure value: re-vectorizing is the safe answer when the manifest cannot vouch for the file. Logged at warning. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_recreate_trinity_file returns the Path it wrote or None; every None (fence refusal, no template, unreadable template, failed write) means 'not recreated', and the success path never returns None: the checker reads the other refusals as success. Each is logged. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_check_vector_deps answers 'are chromadb and numpy confirmed importable'. A check that could not run has not confirmed them, so False is the true answer; the self-report reads it as degraded either way. Logged at warning. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

declared_roots: an unreadable AIPASS_ROOTS.json answers [] (no external roots), logged at error. Never None: ai_mail registry/read.py 474 and drone registry_handler.py 458 loop over the answer outside their try. Not a raise: detector.py 298 (read_scope, feeding health and lint) calls it bare. No caller writes [] out as truth. Rollover's write scope (_read_registry), the push, the todo lane and the normalizer all exclude the external tier. read_scope only reports, and an external name then answers 'Unknown branch', never another branch. Leg 12 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

Both lines are FileNotFoundError: an absent passport declares nothing (None), and an absent declared-roots file declares no roots ([]). That is the answer for an absent file, not a failure value; the unreadable roots branch (470) is not covered here. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision; lines moved in leg 10.

declared_residency: an unreadable passport declares nothing, logged at error. None cannot add or swap a citizen: a core citizen is kept (the sealed registry is the anchor) and a resident candidate is refused, the same policy as for an absent passport. The contract was asked for by @daemon (5031a591), whose scheduler calls it. Leg 10 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_write answers 'written'. False on every path that did not write (fence refusal, failed write); the success path returns True only. The checker reads the fence refusal as success. Logged at error. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_write_json answers 'written'. False on every path that did not write (fence refusal, failed write); the success path returns True only. The checker reads the fence refusal as success. Logged at warning. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_read_ledger merges absent and unreadable on purpose: bump_pending counts both as PENDING ('a missing record of a push is not a record of a push') and its reason names both ('never pushed, or lost'). The unreadable case is logged at error. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

_resolve_branch and _validate_count return None only after _refuse(ctx, ...) has recorded the refusal and its reason; every None is a refusal and no success returns None. The checker reads the other refusals as success. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

handle_command answers 'was this command routed here', not 'did it succeed'. An invalid --n is handled: the error is printed to the user and logged, so True is correct and False would send the router looking for another handler. Leg 8 of DPLAN-0354, @memory's decision.

The stub is the cure (compass 493; @devpulse's leg 11 ruling (a)). Each keeps a far side off the disk or the bus. 93-96 aipass.prax: the real logger writes every module's log file under logs/, and its json service writes operation logs. 120-121 handlers.json.json_handler: log_operation writes memory_json operation logs. 128-131 aipass.trigger: Trigger.fire posts real events to the bus. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Ruling (b): a read, not a patch. The live-state guard reads trinity_push._REPO_ROOT to check that the push lane's own root holds a core registry with rows before a live-fleet test runs. No public name carries that root (registry_scope.REPO_ROOT is the other lane, read beside it), and no door is added for the guard. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

The stub is the cure (ruling (a)). _get_module re-imports config_loader after the fixture evicted the json package, so it binds conftest's json_handler stand-in; with the real one bound, load/save write memory_json operation logs. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Parked tier: vector/embedder.py was parked with the symbolic fragments tier on 2026-08-14 (the owner's ruling) and this file skips; the lines stay as they were. The stub also keeps fastembed from loading a model. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Parked tier: the symbolic fragments tier was parked on 2026-08-14 (the owner's ruling) and this file skips; the lines stay as they were. Where the import is meant to raise (the parked package's __init__ raises), the raise is the test. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.
Parked tier: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-14 keeps this file as it was, and it skips, so these pops never run. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

File-wide by devpulse's leg 12 ruling: each harness (_import_orchestrator, _import_extractor, _import_rollover_module, _import_normalize, _import_line_counter) stands fake handler modules in through monkeypatch.setitem and evicts through monkeypatch, so teardown removes every one. The fakes keep the run off live state: execute_rollover writes .trinity, the backups and the stores; the json package's json_handler writes operation logs; the detector walks the live fleet. The in-function imports bind under conftest's per-test prax/json/trigger stand-ins; at the top of the file they would bind the real logger at collection. The importlib fetches (161/162, 269, 1892, 1919, 2363, 2408, 3237) take the REAL module from the cache for the same reason and patch it at the edge. A lines rule closes a line here (measured on 86, leg 12); file-wide is the ruling. Leg 12 of DPLAN-0354.

File-wide by devpulse's leg 12 ruling: the fixture evicts conftest's json package stand-in through monkeypatch (_evict records each one) and re-imports the REAL config_loader, detector and rollover so the code under test is real; teardown puts the stand-ins back. The other fetches take real modules (todo_roll, todo_report, memory_files, entry_limits, memory, config_content, rollover_config) from the cache under conftest's per-test prax/json stand-ins and patch them at the edge; a top-of-file import would bind the real json shim and logger at collection, and those write operation logs. The display fetches (108 and three in tests) were cured in leg 12: display is imported at the top. Leg 12 of DPLAN-0354.

Ruling (c): reads config_loader._CONFIG_PATH once, BEFORE the fixture repoints it at tmp, so TestOperatorConfigIsolation can prove the operator file is untouched. The contract: every config verb writes the file at _CONFIG_PATH. The far side is memory_json/custom_config/memory.config.json, the live operator config. No public name carries the path, and no door was added for the test. Leg 12 of DPLAN-0354.

Not stubs: each importlib.import_module fetches the REAL module. 54/55 first-import rollover_config and rollover_json before any stand-in lands, because what they bind at import they keep. 107-109 take the real cli flag helpers so the routing guards are real. 203/291 fetch the parent package to evict its cached attribute (monkeypatch restores it). 267/316 fetch the real handlers.cli package to compare with. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

The stub is the cure (ruling (a)). rollover.py imports these at import time, and each far side writes. orchestrator.execute_rollover writes .trinity, the backups and the vector stores. memory_watcher.check_and_rollover runs that same rollover. detector's walk recreates a missing .trinity file. todo_report.roll_pad writes the .backup todo backlogs. plans_processor.process_plans embeds and writes the flow_plans store. 134-137 register the REAL cli flag helpers under the stand-in package, which has no __path__. 139/140 are the parent packages. 207 is the deliberate re-import of rollover against them. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Contracts pinned, each with no public caller that leaves the disk alone. 149/284: detector._read_registry is the rollover WRITE scope (it stops at the repo edge); its public readers walk files and return counts, never rows, and read_scope adds the externals. 228/262: rollover._normalize_rolled never reaches another repository and names a branch whose frame could not be written; its public caller runs a real rollover first. 409: spawn_pusher._write_json refuses a path outside the root; its public caller pushes the spawn templates. 1015: templates._announce_bump fires on the bus; its public caller stamps the receipts. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Contract pinned: the WRITE scope (detector._read_registry) stops at the repo edge while read_scope reaches a declared external. The write scope's public readers (check_all_branches, get_rollover_stats) walk files and return counts, not rows, so the difference is visible only here. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Contract pinned: a declared root is written with forward slashes on Windows. The tests hand _spell a Windows path flavour, which no public caller accepts; the public caller (roots add) writes AIPASS_ROOTS.json under the real home with the host's flavour. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Ruling (b): tp._RULES_CACHE.clear() empties the module's cache of the global rules file so the test reads its own tmp copy and can count re-reads; there is no public reset, and no door is added for the test. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

Contracts pinned on a tmp file: the meta line is tab then template semantics, a refresh restores _usage from the template and never leaves a bare tab, and the receipt is bumped after a refresh (or the refresh succeeds with no receipt). The public caller refreshes every live branch's .trinity files, which is live state. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.

File-wide because no_product_call passes no line (the checklist calls a lines rule inert); it covers TestWhatTheHostCanActuallyHold, lines 660 and 675. Host probes @devpulse asked for. They measure what the running file system holds (case-only names fold or not; a differing stem is always a second file), the premise every case-glob pin in this file is written on. No product code answers that question. Leg 11 of DPLAN-0354.
